en.subtitle: Test your password against 10 attack types and 6 hashing algorithms. No password is stored or transmitted.
en.hint: Local calculation + <abbr title="Have I Been Pwned">HIBP</abbr> k-anonymity check.
en.hibpText: This password appears — times in data breaches indexed by Have I Been Pwned. It is strongly recommended not to use it.
en.hibpPrivacy: Verified via k-anonymity: only the first 5 chars of the SHA-1 hash are sent.
en.hibpSafe: This password does not appear in any known breach from Have I Been Pwned.
en.hibpError: Could not verify against Have I Been Pwned (network issue).
en.tableCaption: Crack time by attack type and hashing algorithm
en.methContent:
10 attack types modeled

1. Brute force — exhaustive. 2. Dictionary — ~14B leaked credentials. 3. Hybrid — dict + rules. 4. Mask — predictable structures. 5. Rainbow table — unsalted hash lookup. 6. Credential stuffing — reuse of leaked pairs. 7. Password spraying — common passwords. 8. Markov — statistical sequences. 9. PCFG — grammatical modeling. 10. Combinator — 2-dictionary concatenation.

6 hashing algorithms

Hashcat on 12× RTX 4090: MD5 ~2,000 GH/s, SHA-1 ~610 GH/s, SHA-256 ~272 GH/s, NTLM ~2,000 GH/s, bcrypt ~71 kH/s, Argon2id ~800 H/s.

Limitations

State/cloud attackers could be 10–1,000× faster. Phishing, keyloggers, SIM swapping bypass password strength entirely.
en.footer: No password is stored. Only network request: first 5 chars of SHA-1 hash sent to HIBP (k-anonymity).
en.beyondUniverse: Longer than the age of the universe
en.resistsBeyond: Resists beyond the age of the universe.
en.bruteSectionLabel: Detail: brute force by hashing algorithm
en.appDescription: Time2Crack calculates locally how long it would take to crack your password, without ever transmitting your password.
